verses.text: “Go quiet before me, you islands. Let the peoples get their strength back. Let them come close and then speak. Let's meet to settle the case.

Who raised someone up from the east? Who called him to his feet in righteousness? He hands nations over to him and puts kings under his rule. He makes them like dust before his sword and stubble blown before his bow.
He chases them and passes through safely, even on roads his feet have never taken before.
Who made it happen and called up generation after generation from the start? I did. I am the LORD, the first, and I'm still the same with the last.”
The islands saw and got scared. The ends of the earth shake. They come closer and gather.
Everyone helps their neighbor and tells their brother, “Stay strong!”

The carpenter gets the goldsmith going. The one smoothing things with a hammer encourages the one striking the anvil. “That joint looks good,” they say, and they nail the idol down so it won't wobble.
“But you, Israel, are my servant. Jacob, I chose you. You're the family of Abraham, my friend.
I took hold of you from the ends of the earth and called you from its farthest corners. I told you, ‘You're my servant. I chose you, and I haven't thrown you away.’
Don't be scared, because I'm with you. Don't panic, because I'm your God. I'll make you strong. I'll help you. I'll hold you up with my righteous right hand.
Look, everyone furious with you will be ashamed and humiliated. The people who fight you will come to nothing and perish.
You'll look for the people who came after you, and you won't find them. Whoever goes to war against you will be like nothing, like they never existed.
I'm the LORD your God. I'll hold your right hand and tell you, ‘Don't be afraid. I'll help you.’
Don't be afraid, Jacob, you little worm, and you people of Israel. I'll help you,” says the LORD. “The Holy One of Israel is the one who redeems you.
Look, I've made you a new threshing tool with sharp teeth. You'll thresh mountains and grind them down, and turn hills into husks.
You'll toss them into the air, and the wind will carry them off. A whirlwind will scatter them. You'll celebrate in the LORD and take pride in the Holy One of Israel.
The poor and needy look for water and can't find any. Their tongues are dry from thirst. I, the LORD, will answer them. I, Israel's God, won't leave them behind.
I'll open up rivers on bare heights and springs in the middle of valleys. I'll turn the wilderness into pools of water and dry land into springs.
I'll plant cedar, acacia, myrtle, and oil trees in the wilderness. I'll put cypress, pine, and box trees together out in the desert.
Then people can see it, know it, think about it, and understand together that the LORD's hand did this. The Holy One of Israel made it happen.
Make your case,” says the LORD. “Bring out your best arguments!” says Jacob's King.
“Let those idols step up and tell us what's going to happen! Tell us what happened before so we can think it through and see where it ended. Or show us what's coming.
Tell us what'll happen from here on so we know you're gods. Go ahead, do something good or something bad. Give us something we can all see and be shaken by.
Look, you're nothing, and your work comes to nothing. Anyone who chooses you is doing something disgusting.
“I raised someone up from the north and he came, someone from where the sun rises who calls on my name. He'll come down on rulers like mortar underfoot, like a potter treading clay.
Who announced this from the start so we could know? Who said it ahead of time so we could say, ‘He was right’? Nobody announced it. Nobody showed us. Nobody heard a word from you.
I was the first to say to Zion, ‘Look, here they are!’ And I'll give Jerusalem someone who brings good news.
I look around and there's nobody. There's no adviser among them who can answer a single word when I ask.
Look at them. All their work is empty and amounts to nothing. Their cast idols are wind and confusion.
